message:
Well it's finally happened.  I've finally been caught in the T-Netix/Evercom/Securus extortion web.  I've been receiving phone calls just fine for a good while.  The little recording at the beginning always said the call was through T-Netix and the cost for the call would be $.85.  I stopped receiving calls almost two weeks ago.  Last night a family member of the inmate called to tell me that my loved one in the MD DoC has been trying to call as usual but has been getting a recording that my line has a block on it.  I called my local provider (Verizon) who said there is no block on my line, but gave me a number for T-Netix anyway.  I also called my long distance provider (AT&T) who said there were two blocks on my line, one being a umsb (usage management systems block) and the other was supposedly from my local provider.  I argued that I'd already spoken to my local provider and they had no blocks on my line.  I was given a number for the umsb block and called it but they were closed for the night. It was an AT&T number.  I called them today and they said there should be no block on my line and that they could see no block on my line.  They also eventually referred me to T-Netix.  I really didn't even want to have to speak to T-Netix as I've been able to avoid them for so long.  I had no choice now so I called them. The fun begins.

 A customer service rep asked for my phone number, then my address, as **she said there was no record of me in the system at all**.  When I was giving her my address, after giving just the house number I hesitated as there was some disturbance here and I didn't think she'd be able to hear me.  Wonder of wonders she vocally completed my address, down to the detail of "Lane".  I asked if they did not have any record of me in the system, how did she know my street name and that my address ended in "Lane"?   Long pause, followed by her answer that while T-Netix had no information on me, Evercom did, and she could see the account Evercom has on me. So "there is no record of you" was lie number 1. She then informed me that I had a block on my phone by Evercom for non-payment of bills and that Evercom has sent two bills to me. More lies.  I have not received any bill from anyone other than Verizon and AT&T and told her so.  Also, my calls have been paid for through those providers.  She then started asking me all sorts of questions about a second phone line I have for my computer.  That line is used for nothing else but my computer to hook up to the internet.  No calls are ever placed or received on it, ever.  How did they get that information and why are they so obsessed with it?  I now fear I may get a block on my computer line and then won't even be able to access the internet. As no call from any correctional institution has ever been received on this line this phone number really is none of their concern, period.  She also asked me if I had any cell phones.  I said no. I wasn't about to give her any more information than she already had.   The csr wouldn't give ME any information let alone any help.  She said all she could do is send in a "trouble ticket" via e-mail to let Evercom know I have not received their bills.  She would not give me a phone number and insisted there is no way to contact anyone in T-Netix, Evercom or Securus by phone except by the number I used to get to her.  She gave me a fax number for Securus and said that is my only recourse.  She says Securus is the parent corporation of T-Netix and Evercom.   I told her I have not only not been billed by anyone, I also have not been contacted by phone by any of the T-Netix/Evercom/Securus people and that it probably is illegal to simply put a block on my phone without contacting me. She repeated that she had no idea why Evercom had my account and that T-Netix should be who handles my account, and that she would send in the trouble ticket and there is nothing else anyone can do and nobody else I can contact other than faxing Securus.   Wonder of wonders, just a few hours later I received my first recorded message telling me I must call them.  What a coincidence! (not)

 The recording was cut off so I don't even know who called, whether it was T-Netix or Evercom.  I called the number (and still did not get any info about who I had called) but stopped using it's automated system when it got to the point that it wanted my social security number.  I'm not sure what my next move will be.  I'm so angry I can't think.  I have very few people in my life at present, and just lost my mother earlier this month due to cancer.  Now because of this corrupt phone company/companies I have lost one of the only other people I have in the world to talk to.  I'm so angry and in such dispair.  I could just spit nails.

Now I know that there are TWO accounts running on me, one with Evercom and one with T-Netix, and that there are two blocks on my house phone line and that they have my computer phone line in their records. I know Evercom says I've been billed twice and not paid my bills.  I have no way to deal with this without giving up my SSN which I don't want to do.  I no doubt will end up being billed by both companies, and it will take forever to straighten that out, if it EVER gets straightened out.  Meanwhile, I've been paying for my calls through my own providers.  If I just did what they want me to I'd end up paying for the same calls three times.  Meanwhile, there's no way for me to talk to my loved one, whose support I desperately need in this time of grief.   I'm just not sure what to do next.
